title: Man Utd Player Ratings vs. Leeds: Red Devils Stop the Rot at Elland Road
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack11:23 AM EDTManchester United shared the spoils at Elland Road.  / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesManchester United were held to a point by historic rivals Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday, as Dominic Calvert-Lewin canceled out Bryan Mbuemo’s opener.

Michael Carrick entered this fixture firmly in the hot seat after a woeful showing against Tottenham Hotspur was followed by defeat in the Champions League at Atlético Madrid. Lisandro Martínez’s postmatch comments all but confirmed United’s state of crisis, and many believed they were underdogs in West Yorkshire, given the impressive start to the season Leeds have made.

Daniel Farke’s side were beaten for the first time this term at Arsenal last weekend, yet they were made to work incredibly hard for a point against the Red Devils. In a throwback affair laden with grit, Man Utd competed fiercely and were good value for their first-half lead.

However, Leeds enjoyed waves of momentum that the visitors struggled to stymie, and Calvert-Lewin is proving inevitable in front of goal at Elland Road. He drew Leeds level from a messy corner sequence, and although there was plenty of time left in the game, both teams seemed pretty content with a point apiece.
There was an absence of big chances late in the game, and Carrick’s side will return to Manchester with something to build on.

Mbeumo delivered from a central position. / Paul ELLIS/AFP/Getty ImagesPlay Bryan Mbeumo centrally, and he will deliver.
The Cameroon international has spent much of the season to date shunted out wide, forced to create separation one-on-one all while limiting his touches in the opposition’s box. It’s not his game.

He worked superbly in tandem with Ivan Toney at Brentford, with the pair particularly proficient on the counterattack, and while his potency in transition has manifested only sporadically in Manchester, Mbeumo has shown that he possesses canny instincts in front of goal.

He missed a gilt-edged chance with his head from an excellent Youri Tielemans delivery, but atoned soon after. The previous mishap was no deterrent for Mbeumo, who finished ever so cleverly from another Tielemans cross, opening up his foot to steer the ball past James Trafford and into the corner.

This wasn’t exactly a standout performance from Man Utd’s goalscorer, who looked dazed and confused during Leeds’ goal sequence, yet the Cameroonian’s strike ultimately meant a result was earned at Elland Road.

Fernandes must’ve just smelt his performance at Elland Road. / Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Images/Getty ImagesMan Utd were pretty impressive as a collective in a tough environment, with Leeds evolving into Chris Wilder’s Sheffield United when they dazzled the Premier League with their marauding center backs in 2019–20.
Carrick should thus be content with a point, even if a lead was surrendered, but United’s gritty result was claimed despite the efforts of their captain.

Bruno Fernandes loves playing against Leeds, yet the very worst of the Portuguese came to play on Sunday afternoon. He was petulant and argumentative, even castigating teammates for making the right decision (see his reaction toward Tielemans after Mbeumo headed his delightful cross wide).
He’s performing as if he knows he’s in a rut, trying to do too much to rediscover his best. At the moment, Fernandes’s apex appears a million miles away.
Mbeumo opened the scoring with a clever finish. / Stu Forster/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Senne Lammens—7.0: Wasn’t much he could’ve done to prevent Calvert-Lewin from restoring parity. While Leeds enjoyed bright spells, they failed to work Man Utd’s goalkeeper.

CB: Leny Yoro—6.9: The young Frenchman is certainly growing in comfort, even if he was asked to perform a different role here. Yoro had no issues defending space as one of the wide center backs in Man Utd’s back three.
CB: Harry Maguire—7.5: There was again no clean sheet for the visitors, although Maguire did deal with Leeds’ distinct threat from crosses rather well.

CB: Lisandro Martínez—6.1: The Argentine remained in the team despite his outburst on Tuesday, but he was only in the limelight for 45 minutes. Martínez was withdrawn at halftime, likely due to injury.
